questions.prompt: In Claude outcomes (beta), what is the default for max_iterations?

options.text: 1, so the agent gets one try and one review of that try
options.explanation: The docs give a default of 3.

options.text: 20, so the agent gets as many tries as the system allows
options.explanation: 20 is the maximum, not the default.

options.text: 3, and the largest value that you can set for it is 20
options.explanation: Right. Claude's docs say the setting is optional, with default 3 and maximum 20.

questions.prompt: What happens in the OpenAI Agents SDK when a run goes past max_turns?

options.text: The SDK quietly adds more turns, so the run always finishes without any error at all
options.explanation: Going over the limit raises an error. It does not add turns.

options.text: It raises MaxTurnsExceeded, unless you gave an error handler to return a final output
options.explanation: Right. The docs say it raises MaxTurnsExceeded, and an error handler can return a controlled final output instead.

options.text: The SDK sends the last file to the client, because the run is judged to be finished
options.explanation: Nothing is sent to anyone. The run ends with the error, or with your handler's output.

questions.prompt: Why does Anthropic say agents often include stopping conditions?

options.text: To make the output look more creative, since a limit forces the model to take risks
options.explanation: Anthropic gives control as the reason, not creativity.

options.text: To maintain control, for example with a maximum number of iterations in the loop
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic says stopping conditions, such as a maximum number of iterations, help maintain control.

options.text: To avoid ever needing a person, since a limit lets the agent finish every task alone
options.explanation: A limit does not remove people. It ends a loop that might otherwise run on.
